stories.headline: Xiaomi reaches frontier AI on $3M, reshaping the build-vs-buy calculus
stories.summary: Xiaomi's MiMo-V2.6-Pro, a mixture-of-experts model with 42 billion active parameters, debuted top of Artificial Analysis's open-weights intelligence ranking. The reinforcement learning run cost $2.6M across 130 hours; weights, training code, and environments are public under MIT licence. If a phone maker reaches frontier open-weight quality at that cost, what does your closed-model contract actually buy?

stories.headline: Meta's new AI agent hands full account control to any local app
stories.summary: Muse, Meta's agentic assistant, holds authenticated access to email, calendar, purchases, and social accounts. stories.headline: NVIDIA's secure inference retains 96% speed on sensitive workloads
stories.summary: Encrypted inference on NVIDIA's Blackwell GPUs retained 96.1–98.2% of baseline throughput in NVIDIA's own tests, with per-token latency under 5% overhead. The gains come from framework-level fixes: smarter memory routing, async token readback, and a kernel-timing correction. Which data residency obligation actually governs your customer-facing deployment: the one your legal team cited, or your regulator's published standard?
stories.take: Secure inference was a performance trade-off; NVIDIA's own numbers put the cost below 4%.

stories.headline: Synthetic edge cases expose where tool-calling agents break beyond happy paths
stories.summary: Tool-calling agents score well on tidy benchmarks but fail on edge cases that violate their own rules. EdgeGen (an arXiv preprint) auto-generates database-grounded edge cases from an agent's spec, no human annotation required. Fine-tuning on EdgeGen data lifted task-progress scores by 2 to 42 percent. Run it against your hardest agent workflow before your next eval cycle.

stories.headline: The AI testing guide built from 700 engineers' real questions
stories.summary: Hamel Husain's FAQ distils questions from over 700 engineers into sharp opinions on what actually works. The core advice: spend 60-80% of development time on error analysis, start by manually reviewing 20-50 outputs, and treat evals as part of development, not a separate budget line. Pull it up when your eval scores stop matching what users experience.

stories.headline: Databricks gives any agent a single governed window into your data estate
stories.summary: Agents querying the same Databricks data from different tools have returned contradictory answers, each carrying stale, hand-modelled definitions. Genie One MCP, now generally available inside Unity Gateway, gives any agent a single governed entry point across structured and unstructured data, with audit logging on every invocation. Add it to any agent already hitting your Lakehouse.

sections.synthesis: This week's practical releases each reduce a different cost that teams had quietly accepted as fixed: inference overhead, token spend on classification, brittle eval suites, guesswork in test design, and contradictory data answers. The common thread is substitution, not augmentation.

stories.headline: Latin America's card fraud rate runs 160% above Europe's
stories.summary: Stripe's analysis of billions of transactions (2022–2026) finds Latin America's card fraud rate ran 160% above Europe's in 2025. Asia Pacific flipped to the lowest-fraud region for the first time, driven by strict 3DS mandates: Malaysia cut fraud 74% in three years. Before entering a new market, price its fraud environment into your margin model.
stories.take: Cross-border fraud risk was assumed uniform; four years of Stripe data shows it varies by 160%.
